summary: preinstall beacon exfiltrates installer host and parent-project identifiers to OAST callback via DNS/HTTP/HTTPS
details: package.json declares a preinstall script that runs index.js on npm install. index.js collects the installer's hostname, username, home directory, current working directory, local/public/resolver IPs, and the consuming project's package.json name/author/repository/homepage, then transmits the JSON payload to the hardcoded external host da51rv0hb2uc72tg4gvgdepinjcallbk1.oast.fun over three channels: an HTTPS POST, an HTTP request, and a DNS tunnel that hex-encodes the payload and splits it into ≤60-character DNS labels under the callback host. Public-IP discovery uses api.ipify.org, icanhazip.com, and ifconfig.me. The DNS-label chunking is a transport designed to survive egress filters that block outbound HTTP. The package's self-description as security research does not change the behavior: installer-side identifiers leave the installer's machine to a third-party OAST/Interactsh host on install without opt-in.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
